headline: Bank Manager Claims ₹17 Crore In Fake Notes Were Just 'High-Yield Investment Decor' To Improve Branch Vastu
body:
The local branch manager arrested this week in connection with the discovery of ₹17.29 crore in counterfeit currency has defended the presence of the notes, claiming they were part of a sophisticated 'energetic balancing' experiment. According to investigators, the manager had meticulously arranged the fake currency into the shape of a giant lotus flower inside the bank's currency chest to align the building's north-east corner with positive financial flows.

'I didn't think of them as fake; I thought of them as metaphysical assets,' the manager reportedly told the internal audit team during questioning. 'The notes were printed on high-gloss stock that reflected the fluorescent lights perfectly, creating an aura of extreme prosperity that supposedly makes the real currency feel more comfortable and prone to multiplying. The vault just wasn't radiating enough wealth before I introduced the paper.'

Branch staff revealed that the manager had been prohibiting any physical access to the chest for months, citing 'meditative silence requirements' for the money. Junior cashiers were instructed to leave offerings of marigold petals at the vault door every morning to ensure the interest rates remained competitive. The National Investigation Agency, while processing the evidence, has noted that the counterfeit notes were remarkably ornate, featuring portraits of historical figures wearing sunglasses and cricket pads instead of the standard official imagery.
caption: Bank manager claims ₹17cr in fake notes were just high-end Vastu decor. We have officially reached peak 'fake it till you make it.' #Banking #Vastu #FakeNotes #Finance #IndiaNews (satire)
